source.title: Polya-Schur-Lax Problems: Hyperbolicity and Stability Preservers — A List of Open Problems

accepted.question_text: Let Phi(t) = 2 * sum_{n=1}^{infinity} (2n^4 pi^2 e^{9t/2} - 3n^2 pi e^{5t/2}) e^{-n^2 pi e^{2t}} and Xi(z) = integral_{-infinity}^{infinity} Phi(t) e^{izt} dt (the completed Riemann xi-function). (i) What number-theoretic information is encoded in integral_0^{infinity} Phi(x) cos(zx) dx? In particular, can the Prime Number Theorem — equivalent to this function having no zeros in {z in C : Im(z) >= 1/2} — be proved using only this integral expression? (ii) Which multiplier sequences (real sequences {gamma_k} such that applying the diagonal operator sum gamma_k a_k x^k to any hyperbolic polynomial sum a_k x^k yields a hyperbolic polynomial) even out the zero spacings of the Xi function? (iii) Does there exist R > 0 such that integral_0^R Phi(x) cos(zx) dx has more than one pair of complex conjugate zeros? (iv) Is differentiation a more effective method than the midpoint method for evening out the spacings of zeros of real entire functions of order 1 with all real zeros?
accepted.context_brief: Number-theoretic and zero-spacing questions about the Riemann xi-function and partial Fourier integrals

evidence.quote: What are the number theoretic aspects hidden in integral_0^infty Phi(x)cos(zx)dx? For instance, is it possible to prove the Prime Number Theorem, equivalent to this function in z having no zeros in {z in C : Im(z) >= 1/2}, using only this integral expression?
Which multiplier sequences even out zero spacings for the Xi function? Does there exist R > 0 such that integral_0^R Phi(x)cos(zx)dx has more than one pair of complex correlated zeros?

accepted.question_text: Let A be a skew-symmetric n x n real matrix and B_1, B_2 positive definite real matrices. It is known that det(A + i(x B_1 + y B_2)) is a stable polynomial (nonzero whenever Im(x) > 0 and Im(y) > 0), with all terms of even degree if n is even and odd degree if n is odd. Is the converse true: if a polynomial in x, y has all terms of even (resp. odd) degree according to n, must it equal det(A + i(x B_1 + y B_2)) for some such A, B_1, B_2?
accepted.context_brief: Converse characterization of determinantal stable polynomials from skew-symmetric and positive definite matrices

evidence.quote: If A is skew symmetric n x n, and B_1, B_2 are positive definite, then det(A + i(xB_1 + yB_2)) is stable, with all terms even degree if n is even and odd degree if n is odd. Is the converse true?

accepted.question_text: Polynomial analogue of the additive Horn problem: Given n and vectors alpha, beta, gamma in R^n, when does there exist a triple (f, g, h) of real-rooted polynomials with roots alpha, beta, gamma respectively, and a homogeneous stable polynomial F(x, y, z) (stable meaning F(x,y,z) != 0 whenever Im(x), Im(y), Im(z) > 0) such that f = F(x, 1, 0), g = F(0, x, 1), h = F(1, 0, x)? It is known that Horn's problem is solvable if and only if (alpha, beta, gamma) is the boundary of a hive, and that the logs of the coefficients of F determine a hive, but this condition is not sufficient. What are necessary and sufficient conditions on f, g, h guaranteeing the existence of such F?
accepted.context_brief: Polynomial analogue of the additive Horn problem via homogeneous stable polynomials

evidence.quote: Polynomial analogue of additive Horn problem: Given n and alpha, beta, gamma in R^n, when does there exist a triple (f,g,h) of real rooted polynomials with roots alpha, beta, gamma and a homogeneous stable polynomial F(x,y,z) such that f=F(x,1,0), g=F(0,x,1), h=F(1,0,x)? Known: Horn's problem is solvable iff (alpha,beta,gamma) is boundary of a hive. Logs of coefficients of F determine a hive, but this is not sufficient. What are necessary and sufficient conditions on f,g,h guaranteeing existence of F?

accepted.question_text: In the Fischer-Fock space F_k with inner product <f,g>_{F_k} = sum_{alpha in N^k} alpha! a(alpha) b(alpha) (where a(alpha), b(alpha) are Taylor coefficients of f and g respectively), define for a real homogeneous polynomial p(z_1,...,z_k) of degree n the capacity Cap(p) = inf_{z_1>0,...,z_k>0} [p(z_1,...,z_k) / (z_1 ... z_k)^{n/k}] * (n! / k^n). For real homogeneous degree-n polynomials p, q in k variables, is it true that <p, q>_{F_k} >= Cap(p) Cap(q) (n! / k^n)?
accepted.context_brief: Fischer-Fock inner product lower bound via capacity for homogeneous polynomials

evidence.quote: For real homogeneous degree n polynomials p, q in k variables, is <p,q>_{F_k} >= Cap(p) Cap(q) n!/k^n?

accepted.question_text: A sequence {gamma_k}_{k in N} of positive reals is called a complex zero decreasing sequence (CZDS) if for every real polynomial sum a_k x^k, the number of non-real zeros of sum gamma_k a_k x^k is at most the number of non-real zeros of sum a_k x^k. Let {gamma_k}_{k in N} be a sequence of positive reals satisfying gamma_k^2 >= 4 gamma_{k+1} gamma_{k-1} for all k. Is {gamma_k} necessarily a CZDS?
accepted.context_brief: Whether a quadratic growth condition on a positive sequence implies it is a CZDS

evidence.quote: Let Gamma = {gamma_k}_{k in N} be positive and satisfy gamma_k^2 >= 4 gamma_{k+1} gamma_{k-1} for all k. Is Gamma a CZDS?

accepted.question_text: Let Xi(z) = integral_{-infinity}^{infinity} Phi(t) e^{izt} dt where Phi(t) = 2 sum_{n=1}^{infinity} (2n^4 pi^2 e^{9t/2} - 3n^2 pi e^{5t/2}) e^{-n^2 pi e^{2t}} (related to the Riemann xi-function). Define Xi_lambda(z) = integral_{-infinity}^{infinity} Phi(t) e^{lambda t^2} e^{izt} dt. (i) Is it true that for any lambda < 0, almost all zeros of Xi_lambda(z) are real? An affirmative answer would imply that almost all complex zeros of the Riemann zeta function lie on the critical line. (ii) Suppose f is a real entire function of order 1 and maximal type, even, with all zeros in the strip {z : |Im(z)| <= Delta}. Is it true that for every lambda > 0, all but finitely many zeros of e^{-lambda D^2} f (where D = d/dx) are real and simple? Note: the source confirms an affirmative answer to (ii) for the specific functions Xi, Phi, H (defined via the Riemann zeta and Dirichlet L-functions); the general question for arbitrary f remains open.
accepted.context_brief: Zeros of xi-function deformations and entire functions under heat-operator perturbation; connection to Riemann Hypothesis

evidence.quote: Is it true that for any lambda < 0, almost all zeros of Xi_lambda(z) are real? If true, almost all complex zeros of the Riemann zeta function are on the critical line.

Suppose f is real entire of order 1 and maximal type, even, with zeros in strip {z : |Im z| <= Delta}. Is it true that for every lambda > 0, all but finitely many zeros of e^{-lambda D^2} f are real and simple?

accepted.question_text: Let Omega be a subset of C and pi(Omega) the class of all univariate polynomials (with complex coefficients) whose zeros all lie in Omega. Characterize all linear operators T : pi(Omega) -> pi(Omega) union {0}.
accepted.context_brief: Characterization of linear zero-preserving operators on polynomials with zeros in a region

evidence.quote: Characterize all linear operators T : pi(Omega) -> pi(Omega) union {0}.

accepted.question_text: Let Omega be a subset of C, pi_n the vector space of polynomials of degree at most n, and pi_n(Omega) the subclass of pi_n whose zeros all lie in Omega. Describe all linear operators T : pi_n(Omega) -> pi(Omega) union {0} for each n in N.
accepted.context_brief: Characterization of linear operators mapping degree-bounded polynomials with zeros in Omega to polynomials with zeros in Omega

evidence.quote: Describe all linear operators T : pi_n(Omega) -> pi(Omega) union {0} for n in N.

accepted.question_text: Problems 7 and 8 ask to characterize all linear operators T : pi(Omega) -> pi(Omega) union {0} (respectively T : pi_n(Omega) -> pi(Omega) union {0}) where pi(Omega) is the class of polynomials with all zeros in Omega and pi_n(Omega) is its degree-at-most-n subclass. The cases where Omega is a closed circular domain or its boundary are completely solved. Settle these problems for each of the following remaining cases: (a) Omega is an open circular domain (open disk, half-plane, or complement of a closed disk); (b) Omega is a sector or double sector; (c) Omega is a strip; (d) Omega is a half-line.
accepted.context_brief: Settling the linear zero-preserver characterization for specific open domains: circular, sector, strip, half-line

evidence.quote: Settle Problems 7-8 when: (a) Omega is an open circular domain; (b) Omega is a sector or double sector; (c) Omega is a strip; (d) Omega is a half-line.
completely solved for all closed circular domains and boundaries; multivariate finite-order extensions obtained. Remaining open cases listed in Problem 9.

accepted.question_text: Every linear operator T on C[z] has a unique formal differential representation T = sum_{k=0}^{infinity} Q_k(z) (d^k/dz^k) where Q_k are polynomials in C[z]. For a given region Omega subset C, characterize the sequences of polynomials (Q_k) such that T maps pi_n(Omega) into pi(Omega) union {0} for every n in N, where pi_n(Omega) is the class of polynomials of degree at most n with all zeros in Omega.
accepted.context_brief: Characterization of coefficient polynomials Q_k in the differential representation of a linear zero-preserver

evidence.quote: Every linear operator T on C[z] has unique formal differential representation T = sum_{k=0}^{infty} Q_k(z) d^k/dz^k, Q_k in C[z]. Characterize the polynomials Q_k such that T : pi_n(Omega) -> pi(Omega) union {0} for n in N.

accepted.question_text: Let pi_n denote the space of real polynomials of degree at most n, and for a real polynomial p let Z_c(p) denote the number of non-real zeros of p counted with multiplicity. Characterize all linear operators T : pi_n -> pi_n such that Z_c(T[p(x)]) <= Z_c(p(x)) for every real polynomial p in pi_n.
accepted.context_brief: Characterization of linear operators on real polynomials that do not increase the count of non-real zeros

evidence.quote: Characterize all linear operators T : pi_n -> pi_n such that Z_c(T[p(x)]) <= Z_c(p(x)), where p, T[p] are real polynomials and Z_c counts non-real zeros with multiplicity.

accepted.question_text: Let V be a cone in R^n and H_n(V) the set of real homogeneous polynomials in n variables that are hyperbolic with respect to every direction e in V (meaning f(e) != 0 and the univariate polynomial t -> f(alpha + te) has only real zeros for every alpha in R^n). Describe all linear operators T on R[z_1,...,z_n] such that T maps H_n(V) into H_n(V) union {0}.
accepted.context_brief: Characterization of linear operators preserving hyperbolicity with respect to a cone

evidence.quote: Let V be a cone in R^n, and H_n(V) the homogeneous polynomials hyperbolic with respect to every e in V. Describe all linear operators T on R[z_1,...,z_n] such that T : H_n(V) -> H_n(V) union {0}.

accepted.question_text: Stable Lax Conjecture 1: Let P(x_0,...,x_m) be a real homogeneous polynomial that is hyperbolic with respect to c = (c_0,...,c_m) in R^{m+1} (meaning P(c) != 0 and t -> P(alpha + tc) has only real zeros for every alpha in R^{m+1}), and let L be a real linear form with L(c) != 0. Does there exist N in N such that L(x_0,...,x_m)^N P(x_0,...,x_m) = det(x_0 A_0 + x_1 A_1 + ... + x_m A_m) for real symmetric matrices A_0,...,A_m satisfying c_0 A_0 + c_1 A_1 + ... + c_m A_m > 0 (positive definite)? Note: the analog of the Lax conjecture for hyperbolic polynomials in four or more variables fails; this stable version remains open.
accepted.context_brief: Stable Lax Conjecture 1: determinantal representation of hyperbolic polynomials after multiplication by a linear factor

evidence.quote: Let P(x_0,...,x_m) be real homogeneous and hyperbolic with respect to c=(c_0,...,c_m), and L a real linear form with L(c) != 0. Does there exist N in N such that L(x_0,...,x_m)^N P(x_0,...,x_m) = det(x_0 A_0 + x_1 A_1 + ... + x_m A_m) for real symmetric matrices A_0,...,A_m with c_0 A_0 + ... + c_m A_m > 0?
analog of Lax conjecture for hyperbolic polynomials in four or more variables fails; Stable Lax Conjecture 1 remains posed.

accepted.question_text: Stable Lax Conjecture 2: For n x n matrices A_1,...,A_m, define eta(A_1,...,A_m) = sum over partitions (S_1,...,S_m) of {1,...,n} of det(A_1[S_1]) ... det(A_m[S_m]), where A_j[S_j] denotes the submatrix of A_j with rows and columns indexed by S_j. A positive pencil is a matrix-valued linear form L_j(z) = sum_{k=1}^{ell} A_{jk} z_k + B_j where each A_{jk} is positive semidefinite and B_j is Hermitian. Is it true that for every real stable polynomial f of degree n in ell variables (stable meaning f(z_1,...,z_ell) != 0 whenever Im(z_i) > 0 for all i), there exist m and positive pencils L_1,...,L_m of this form such that f = eta(L_1,...,L_m)?
accepted.context_brief: Stable Lax Conjecture 2: representation of real stable polynomials via the eta-function of positive pencils

evidence.quote: Is it true that if f is a real stable polynomial of degree n in ell variables, then there exist m and pencils L_j of this form such that f = eta(L_1,...,L_m)?

accepted.question_text: Stable Lax Conjecture 3: Let f be a real stable homogeneous polynomial of degree n in ell variables (stable meaning f(z_1,...,z_ell) != 0 whenever Im(z_i) > 0 for all i). Using the same eta-function and positive pencil notation as in Stable Lax Conjecture 2 (with A_{jk} positive semidefinite), is it true that there exist m and positive pencils L_j with B_j = 0 (purely linear pencils) such that f = eta(L_1,...,L_m)?
accepted.context_brief: Stable Lax Conjecture 3: representation of real stable homogeneous polynomials via purely linear positive pencils

evidence.quote: Let f be real stable homogeneous of degree n in ell variables. Is it true that there exist m and pencils L_j as above with B_j = 0 such that f = eta(L_1,...,L_m)?

accepted.question_text: The Laguerre-Polya class LP_2 consists of entire functions in two complex variables that arise as limits of polynomials with all zeros real (in the appropriate multivariate sense). Are there Lax-type infinite determinantal representations for functions in LP_2? Specifically, is every function in LP_2 expressible as the Weinstein-Aronszajn determinant of a pencil of infinite Hermitian or positive definite matrices?
accepted.context_brief: Determinantal representations for bivariate Laguerre-Polya entire functions

evidence.quote: Are there Lax-type infinite determinantal representations for functions in LP_2? For instance, is every function in LP_2 given by the Weinstein-Aronszajn determinant of a pencil of infinite Hermitian/positive definite matrices?

accepted.question_text: Let P_n be the ring of real polynomials in n variables, P_n^+ the subset of nonnegative polynomials, S_n the subset of sums of squares of polynomials (so S_n is a subset of P_n^+), and M_n the set of finite-order linear partial differential operators with constant real coefficients T on R[z_1,...,z_n] such that T(S_n) is a subset of P_n^+. Is it true that M_n * S_n = P_n^+ for all n? Equivalently, given any nonnegative polynomial P in P_n^+, do there exist a sum-of-squares polynomial S in S_n and an operator T in M_n such that P = T(S)?
accepted.context_brief: Analog of Hilbert's 17th problem: representing nonneg polynomials as differential operators applied to sums of squares

evidence.quote: Is M_n * S_n = P_n^+ for all n? Equivalently, given P in P_n^+, do there exist S in S_n, T in M_n with P = T(S)?

accepted.question_text: A sequence {gamma_k}_{k=0}^{infinity} of real numbers is called a complex zero decreasing sequence (CZDS) if for every real polynomial p(x) = sum_{k=0}^n a_k x^k, the number of non-real zeros (counted with multiplicity) of sum_{k=0}^n gamma_k a_k x^k is at most the number of non-real zeros of p(x). Characterize all CZDS.
accepted.context_brief: Characterization of all complex zero decreasing sequences

evidence.quote: A sequence {gamma_k}_{k=0}^infty is CZDS if it decreases the number of non-real zeros of every real polynomial. Characterize all CZDS.

accepted.question_text: A multiplier sequence is a real sequence T = {gamma_k}_{k=0}^{infinity} such that if p(x) = sum a_k x^k is a hyperbolic polynomial (all zeros real), then T[p] = sum gamma_k a_k x^k is also hyperbolic. A CZDS (complex zero decreasing sequence) is a sequence such that sum gamma_k a_k x^k has at most as many non-real zeros as sum a_k x^k for every real polynomial. Characterize the multiplier sequences that are also CZDS.
accepted.context_brief: Characterization of multiplier sequences that are also complex zero decreasing sequences

evidence.quote: Characterize the multiplier sequences that are CZDS.

accepted.question_text: It is known that for each integer p >= 3, the sequence {e^{-k^p}}_{k=0}^{infinity} is a multiplier sequence (meaning it maps hyperbolic polynomials to hyperbolic polynomials under diagonal action sum e^{-k^p} a_k x^k). Are these sequences also complex zero decreasing sequences (CZDS), i.e., does applying the diagonal operator sum e^{-k^p} a_k x^k to any real polynomial sum a_k x^k not increase the number of non-real zeros?
accepted.context_brief: Whether the multiplier sequences {e^{-k^p}} for integer p >= 3 are also CZDS

evidence.quote: It is known that {e^{-k^p}}_{k=0}^{infty}, where p >= 3 is an integer, is a multiplier sequence. Are these multiplier sequences CZDS?

accepted.question_text: Define moments b_k = integral_0^{infinity} t^{2k} Phi(t) dt and gamma_k = (k! / (2k)!) b_k, where Phi(t) = 2 sum_{n=1}^{infinity} (2n^4 pi^2 e^{9t/2} - 3n^2 pi e^{5t/2}) e^{-n^2 pi e^{2t}} is the function whose Fourier transform gives the Riemann xi-function. Set F(x) = sum_{k=0}^{infinity} (b_k / (2k)!) x^k = integral_0^{infinity} Phi(t) cosh(t sqrt(x)) dt. The Riemann Hypothesis holds if and only if {gamma_k} is a multiplier sequence (equivalently, {gamma_k / k!} is totally positive), and also if and only if {F(k)}_{k=0}^{infinity} is a CZDS. Furthermore, F(k) = (pi^{-1/4} / 64) (k-1) pi^{-sqrt(k)/4} Gamma(1/4 + sqrt(k)/4) zeta(1/2 + sqrt(k)/2). What can be proved about whether {gamma_k} is a multiplier sequence or {F(k)} is a CZDS, and what does this imply for the Riemann Hypothesis?
accepted.context_brief: Multiplier sequence and CZDS formulations equivalent to the Riemann Hypothesis

evidence.quote: The Riemann Hypothesis holds iff {gamma_k} is a multiplier sequence, equivalently {gamma_k/k!} is totally positive.
RH holds iff {F(k)}_{k=0}^infty is a CZDS. Also, F(k) = pi^{-1/4}/64 * (k-1) pi^{-sqrt(k)/4} Gamma(1/4 + sqrt(k)/4) zeta(1/2 + sqrt(k)/2).

accepted.question_text: A multiplier sequence is a real sequence {gamma_k}_{k=0}^{infinity} with gamma_k > 0 such that applying the diagonal operator sum gamma_k a_k x^k to any hyperbolic polynomial sum a_k x^k yields a hyperbolic polynomial. A lambda-sequence (positive definite sequence) is a sequence of nonzero reals {lambda_k} such that sum lambda_k a_k x^k is strictly positive on R whenever sum a_k x^k is strictly positive on R. Characterize all multiplier sequences {gamma_k}_{k=0}^{infinity} with gamma_k > 0 whose reciprocal sequences {1/gamma_k} are lambda-sequences.
accepted.context_brief: Characterization of multiplier sequences whose reciprocals are lambda-sequences

evidence.quote: Characterize multiplier sequences {gamma_k}_{k=0}^infty, gamma_k > 0, whose reciprocal sequences {1/gamma_k} are lambda-sequences.

accepted.question_text: Let phi(x) = sum_{k=0}^{infinity} (gamma_k / k!) x^k with gamma_k >= 0 be a transcendental real entire function of exponential type with only real negative zeros. If lim_{k -> infinity} gamma_k^{1/k} = 0, is {gamma_k} necessarily a complex zero decreasing sequence (CZDS), i.e., does sum_{k=0}^n gamma_k a_k x^k have at most as many non-real zeros as sum_{k=0}^n a_k x^k for every real polynomial?
accepted.context_brief: Whether a zero-type condition on the generating function implies the coefficient sequence is CZDS

evidence.quote: Let phi(x) = sum_{k=0}^infty (gamma_k/k!) x^k, gamma_k >= 0, be transcendental real entire of exponential type with only real negative zeros. If lim_{k->infty} gamma_k^{1/k} = 0, is {gamma_k} a CZDS?

accepted.question_text: Characterize all meromorphic functions F(x) = phi(x)/psi(x) (where phi, psi are entire) such that for every real polynomial sum_{k=0}^n a_k x^k with only real zeros, the polynomial sum_{k=0}^n F(k) a_k x^k also has only real zeros.
accepted.context_brief: Characterization of meromorphic functions F such that the diagonal operator with weights F(k) preserves real-rootedness

evidence.quote: Characterize meromorphic functions F(x) = phi(x)/psi(x) where phi, psi are entire, such that sum_{k=0}^n F(k) a_k x^k has only real zeros whenever sum_{k=0}^n a_k x^k has only real zeros.

accepted.question_text: Characterize all meromorphic functions F(x) such that whenever sum_{k=0}^{infinity} a_k (x^k / k!) is a transcendental entire function with only real zeros, the function sum_{k=0}^{infinity} F(k) a_k (x^k / k!) is also a transcendental entire function with only real zeros, or has all zeros in the half-plane Re(z) < 0.
accepted.context_brief: Characterization of meromorphic F preserving real-rootedness or left-half-plane zeros for entire functions in exponential series form

evidence.quote: Characterize meromorphic F(x) such that sum_{k=0}^infty F(k) a_k x^k/k! is transcendental entire with only real zeros, or all zeros in Re z < 0, whenever sum_{k=0}^infty a_k x^k/k! has only real zeros.

accepted.question_text: A meromorphic Laguerre multiplier sequence is a multiplier sequence of the form {F(k)}_{k=0}^{infinity} where F is a meromorphic function. A multiplier sequence {gamma_k} maps hyperbolic polynomials (all zeros real) to hyperbolic polynomials under diagonal action. A CZDS (complex zero decreasing sequence) satisfies: sum gamma_k a_k x^k has at most as many non-real zeros as sum a_k x^k for every real polynomial. If {F(k)}_{k=0}^{infinity} is a meromorphic Laguerre multiplier sequence, is {F(k)} necessarily a CZDS?
accepted.context_brief: Whether every meromorphic Laguerre multiplier sequence is a CZDS

evidence.quote: If {F(k)}_{k=0}^infty is a meromorphic Laguerre multiplier sequence, is {F(k)} a CZDS?

accepted.question_text: The Wright function is defined by _p Psi_q(x) = sum_{k=0}^{infinity} [prod_{j=1}^p Gamma(a_j k + b_j)] / [prod_{j=1}^q Gamma(c_j k + d_j)] * (x^k / k!). For b_j = d_j = 1 this reduces to the generalized hypergeometric function _p F_q(a_1,...,a_p; b_1,...,b_q; x) = sum_{k=0}^{infinity} [(a_1)_k ... (a_p)_k] / [(b_1)_k ... (b_q)_k] * (x^k / k!). What can be determined about the distribution of zeros of entire Wright functions and generalized hypergeometric functions?
accepted.context_brief: Distribution of zeros of entire Wright functions and generalized hypergeometric functions

evidence.quote: Obtain information about distribution of zeros of entire Wright functions and generalized hypergeometric functions.

accepted.question_text: Consider the Wright-type function _2 Psi_1(x) = sum_{k=0}^{infinity} [Gamma(ak+1) Gamma(bk+1)] / [Gamma(ck+d+1)] * (x^k / k!) with parameters a, b, c, d >= 0 and c >= a + b. Under what additional restrictions on a, b, c, d does _2 Psi_1(x) have only real negative zeros?
accepted.context_brief: Conditions on parameters for a Wright-type function to have only real negative zeros

evidence.quote: Consider _2 Psi_1(x) = sum_{k=0}^infty [Gamma(ak+1)Gamma(bk+1)/Gamma(ck+d+1)] x^k/k!, a,b,c,d >= 0, c >= a+b. Under what additional restrictions on a,b,c,d does _2 Psi_1(x) have only real negative zeros?

accepted.question_text: In the Wright-type function _2 Psi_1(x) from Problem 28, set a = m, b = 0, c = m+1, d = -1, giving f_m(x) = sum_{k=0}^{infinity} [Gamma(mk+1) / Gamma((m+1)k+1)] * (x^k / k!) for m = 0, 1, 2, .... It is known that f_0(x) = J_0(2 sqrt(x)) (the Bessel function of order zero) and f_1(x) = cosh(sqrt(x)) both have only real zeros. For integers m >= 2, f_m has order 1/2. Does f_m(x) have only real zeros for all integers m >= 2?
accepted.context_brief: Whether a specific family of Wright-type entire functions of order 1/2 has only real zeros

evidence.quote: Known: f_0(x) = J_0(2 sqrt x) and f_1(x) = cosh(sqrt x) have only real zeros. For integers m >= 2, f_m has order 1/2. Does f_m(x) have only real zeros?

accepted.question_text: The Jacobi polynomial P_n^{(alpha,beta)}(x) = (1/2^n) sum_{k=0}^n C(n+alpha,k) C(n+beta,n-k) (x-1)^{n-k} (x+1)^k for alpha, beta > -1. Define phi_n(x) = sum_{k=0}^{floor(n/2)} (d^{2k}/dx^{2k} P_n^{(alpha,beta)}(x))|_{x=1} * x^k and psi_n(x) = sum_{k=0}^{floor(n/2)} (d^{2k+1}/dx^{2k+1} P_n^{(alpha,beta)}(x))|_{x=1} * x^k. It is known that for n >= 2, -1 < alpha <= 1, beta > -1, both phi_n(x) and psi_n(x) have only real simple negative zeros. Conjecture: for n >= 4, the zeros of phi_n and phi_{n-1} interlace, and the zeros of psi_n and psi_{n-2} interlace. Is this conjecture true?
accepted.context_brief: Interlacing conjecture for zeros of even and odd derivative evaluations of Jacobi polynomials

evidence.quote: Conjecture: for n >= 4, zeros of phi_n and phi_{n-1} interlace, and zeros of psi_n and psi_{n-2} interlace.

accepted.question_text: Characterize all real polynomials p_n(x) of degree n with all zeros in the open interval (-1, 1) such that the polynomial phi_n(x) = sum_{k=0}^{floor(n/2)} p_n^{(2k)}(1) x^k (formed from the even-order derivatives of p_n evaluated at 1) has only real negative zeros.
accepted.context_brief: Characterization of polynomials with zeros in (-1,1) whose even-derivative evaluation polynomial has only real negative zeros

evidence.quote: Characterize all real polynomials p_n(x) of degree n, all zeros in (-1,1), such that phi_n(x) = sum_{k=0}^{floor(n/2)} p_n^{(2k)}(1) x^k has only real negative zeros.

accepted.question_text: De Bruijn proved: if f is a real entire function of order less than 2 with all zeros in the strip S(Delta) = {z in C : |Im(z)| <= Delta}, then the zeros of cos(lambda D) f(x) (where D = d/dx and cos(lambda D) = sum_{k=0}^{infinity} (-1)^k lambda^{2k} D^{2k} / (2k)!) satisfy |Im(z)| <= sqrt(Delta^2 - lambda^2) when Delta > lambda, and are all real when 0 <= Delta <= lambda. Is there an analog of Jensen's theorem for phi(lambda D) f(x) when phi is a more general transcendental entire function (not just cosine)?
accepted.context_brief: Analog of Jensen's theorem for general entire function operators applied to strip-zero entire functions

evidence.quote: De Bruijn proved: if f is real entire of order less than 2, zeros in strip S(Delta) = {z : |Im z| <= Delta}, then zeros of cos(lambda D)f(x) satisfy |Im z| <= sqrt(Delta^2 - lambda^2) if Delta > lambda, and are real if 0 <= Delta <= lambda. Question: Is there an analog of Jensen's theorem for phi(lambda D)f(x) when phi is a more general transcendental entire function?

accepted.question_text: Consider the finite Fourier transform H_R(x) = integral_0^R Phi(t) cos(xt) dt, where Phi(t) = sum_{n=1}^{infinity} (2 pi^2 n^4 e^{9t} - 3 pi n^2 e^{5t}) exp(-pi n^2 e^{4t}) (a function related to the Riemann xi-function). (i) If R is sufficiently large, are all zeros of H_R(x) located in the strip |Im(z)| < 1? (ii) For what values of R > 0.11, if any, does H_R(x) have non-real zeros? It is known that for 0 < R < 0.11, H_R has only real zeros.
accepted.context_brief: Zero distribution of finite Fourier transforms of the Phi function related to the Riemann xi-function

evidence.quote: If R is sufficiently large, are zeros of H_R(x) located in the strip |Im z| < 1? For what R > 0.11, if any, does H_R(x) have non-real zeros? Known: for 0 < R < 0.11, H_R has only real zeros.

accepted.question_text: Let gamma_k = k^{sqrt(k)} for k >= 1. For each m >= 1, define f_m(x) = sum_{k=0}^{infinity} (gamma_{k+m} / k!) x^k, which is a real entire function of order 1 satisfying f_1^{(m)} = f_{m+1}. For all sufficiently large m, is the sequence {gamma_{k+m}}_{k=1}^{infinity} a multiplier sequence (i.e., does the diagonal operator sum gamma_{k+m} a_k x^k map every hyperbolic polynomial sum a_k x^k to a hyperbolic polynomial)?
accepted.context_brief: Whether shifted sequences of k^{sqrt(k)} are multiplier sequences for large shifts

evidence.quote: Let gamma_k = k^{sqrt k}, k >= 1. For each m >= 1, f_m(x) = sum_{k=0}^infty (gamma_{k+m}/k!) x^k is real entire of order 1, and f_1^{(m)} = f_{m+1}. For all sufficiently large m, is {gamma_{k+m}}_{k=1}^infty a multiplier sequence?

accepted.question_text: Characterize all symmetric, real stable, homogeneous polynomials of degree d in n variables, where a polynomial f in R[z_1,...,z_n] is real stable if f(z_1,...,z_n) != 0 whenever Im(z_i) > 0 for all i. In particular, is it true that for every such polynomial p(z_1,...,z_n), there exists a d x d positive semidefinite matrix A such that p(z_1,...,z_n) = eta(z_1 A,...,z_n A), where eta(A_1,...,A_n) = sum over partitions (S_1,...,S_n) of {1,...,d} of det(A_1[S_1]) ... det(A_n[S_n])? This is open even for n = 2.
accepted.context_brief: Characterization and determinantal representation of symmetric real stable homogeneous polynomials

evidence.quote: Characterize all symmetric, real stable, homogeneous polynomials of degree d in n variables. Is it true that if p is such a polynomial, then there is a d x d positive semidefinite matrix A such that p(z_1,...,z_n) = eta(z_1 A,...,z_n A)? This is not obvious even for n = 2.

accepted.question_text: Let p be a symmetric, real stable, homogeneous polynomial of degree d in n variables with d <= n, having at least one positive coefficient in the monomial basis. Write p(z_1,...,z_n) = sum_{lambda |- d} a_lambda s_lambda(z_1,...,z_n) in the Schur polynomial basis. Is p Schur-positive, i.e., is a_lambda >= 0 for all partitions lambda of d?
accepted.context_brief: Schur-positivity of symmetric real stable homogeneous polynomials

evidence.quote: Let p be symmetric, real stable, homogeneous of degree d in n variables, with d <= n, and suppose p has at least one positive coefficient in the monomial basis. Is p Schur-positive? That is, if p(z_1,...,z_n) = sum_{lambda |- d} a_lambda s_lambda(z_1,...,z_n), is a_lambda >= 0 for all lambda |- d?

accepted.question_text: Stable Schur's Inequality: Let p be a symmetric, real stable, homogeneous polynomial of degree d in n variables with d <= n and at least one positive monomial coefficient. Write p = sum_{lambda |- d} a_lambda s_lambda in the Schur basis. Is it true that a_lambda >= f^lambda a_{(d)} for all partitions lambda of d, where f^lambda is the number of standard Young tableaux of shape lambda and (d) denotes the single-row partition of d?
accepted.context_brief: Stable analog of Schur's inequality: lower bound on Schur coefficients of symmetric real stable homogeneous polynomials

evidence.quote: Is a_lambda >= f^lambda a_{(d)} for all lambda |- d, where f^lambda is the number of standard Young tableaux of shape lambda?

accepted.question_text: Stable Permanent-On-Top Inequality: Let p be a symmetric, real stable, homogeneous polynomial of degree d in n variables with d <= n and at least one positive monomial coefficient. Write p = sum_{lambda |- d} a_lambda s_lambda in the Schur basis. Is it true that a_lambda <= f^lambda a_{(1^d)} for all partitions lambda of d, where f^lambda is the number of standard Young tableaux of shape lambda and (1^d) denotes the single-column partition of d? An affirmative answer would imply Lieb's Permanent-On-Top conjecture.
accepted.context_brief: Stable Permanent-On-Top inequality: upper bound on Schur coefficients implying Lieb's conjecture

evidence.quote: Is a_lambda <= f^lambda a_{(1^d)} for all lambda |- d? An affirmative answer would imply Lieb's Permanent-On-Top conjecture.

accepted.question_text: BMV Conjecture: Let n be a positive integer and A, B arbitrary positive definite n x n real matrices. For any positive integer k, does the function z -> Tr((A + zB)^k) have only nonnegative coefficients as a polynomial in z?
accepted.context_brief: Bessis-Moussa-Villani (BMV) conjecture on nonnegativity of coefficients of Tr((A+zB)^k)

evidence.quote: Let n in N, and A, B be arbitrary positive definite n x n matrices. Then for any k in N, does z -> Tr((A+zB)^k) have only nonnegative coefficients?

accepted.question_text: Suppose f in R[z_1, z_2] is a real stable polynomial (nonzero whenever Im(z_1) > 0 and Im(z_2) > 0) with f(0,0) = 1 and all Taylor coefficients nonnegative. Is it true that the function (z_1, z_2) -> -log(f(-z_1, -z_2)) has all nonnegative Taylor coefficients? This statement is equivalent to the BMV conjecture.
accepted.context_brief: Nonnegativity of Taylor coefficients of -log(f(-z_1,-z_2)) for real stable f; equivalent to BMV conjecture

evidence.quote: Suppose f in R[z_1,z_2] is real stable, f(0,0)=1, and all Taylor coefficients of f are nonneg. Is it true that (z_1,z_2) -> -log(f(-z_1,-z_2)) has all nonneg Taylor coefficients? Equivalent to BMV conjecture.

accepted.question_text: Let p be a real homogeneous polynomial that is hyperbolic with respect to e in R^n (meaning p(e) != 0 and t -> p(alpha + te) has only real zeros for every alpha in R^n), normalized so that p(e) = 1. Let C_p(e)^+ denote the positivity cone of p with respect to e (the connected component of {x in R^n : p(x) != 0} containing e). Suppose v_1, v_2 are in C_p(e)^+. Are all Taylor coefficients of (z_1, z_2) -> -log(p(e - z_1 v_1 - z_2 v_2)) nonnegative? This statement is equivalent to the BMV conjecture.
accepted.context_brief: Nonnegativity of Taylor coefficients of -log(p(e - z_1 v_1 - z_2 v_2)) for hyperbolic p; equivalent to BMV conjecture

evidence.quote: Let p be e-hyperbolic with p(e)=1, e in R^n, and suppose v_1, v_2 are in the positivity cone C_p(e)^+. Are all Taylor coefficients of (z_1,z_2) -> -log(p(e-z_1 v_1 - z_2 v_2)) nonneg? Equivalent to BMV conjecture.

accepted.question_text: A multi-affine polynomial is one of degree at most one in each variable. A Rayleigh polynomial is a multi-affine f in R[z_1,...,z_n] with nonneg coefficients satisfying (partial f / partial z_i)(x) * (partial f / partial z_j)(x) >= (partial^2 f / partial z_i partial z_j)(x) * f(x) for all x in R_+^n and all 1 <= i < j <= n. The original Big Conjecture that all Rayleigh polynomials have log-concave diagonal specializations was disproved for n >= 20. Describe, in terms of Rayleigh-type correlation conditions, a natural class RN_n of multi-affine polynomials in n variables with nonneg coefficients such that if f is in RN_n and Delta(f)(t) = sum_{k=0}^n C(n,k) c_k t^k is the diagonal specialization of f, then (c_k)_{k=0}^n is log-concave with no internal zeros.
accepted.context_brief: Finding a natural subclass of multi-affine polynomials with Rayleigh-type conditions that guarantees log-concavity of diagonal specializations

evidence.quote: Describe, in terms of Rayleigh-type correlations, a natural class RN_n of multi-affine polynomials in n variables with nonneg coefficients such that if f in RN_n and Delta(f)(t) = sum_{k=0}^n C(n,k) c_k t^k is the diagonal specialization of f, then (c_k)_{k=0}^n is log-concave with no internal zeros.
original Big Conjecture for all Rayleigh polynomials was disproved for n >= 20.

accepted.question_text: A Rayleigh matrix is a P-matrix (square matrix with all principal minors positive) A such that f_A(z) = det(A + diag(z_1,...,z_n)) is a Rayleigh polynomial (a multi-affine polynomial with nonneg coefficients satisfying the Rayleigh correlation inequalities). The Big Conjecture that Rayleigh polynomials have log-concave diagonal specializations was disproved for n >= 20. Does f_A(z) = det(A + diag(z_1,...,z_n)) satisfy the conclusion of the Big Conjecture (log-concavity of diagonal specialization coefficients) whenever A is a Rayleigh matrix?
accepted.context_brief: Whether determinantal polynomials of Rayleigh matrices satisfy the log-concavity conclusion of the disproved Big Conjecture

evidence.quote: Does f_A(z) = det(A+Z) satisfy the conclusion of Conjecture 1 whenever A is Rayleigh?

accepted.question_text: A Rayleigh matrix is an n x n P-matrix (all principal minors positive) A such that f_A(z) = det(A + diag(z_1,...,z_n)) is a Rayleigh polynomial (a multi-affine polynomial with nonneg coefficients satisfying (partial f / partial z_i)(x) * (partial f / partial z_j)(x) >= (partial^2 f / partial z_i partial z_j)(x) * f(x) for all x in R_+^n). Describe all n x n Rayleigh matrices.
accepted.context_brief: Characterization of all Rayleigh matrices

evidence.quote: Describe all n x n Rayleigh matrices.

accepted.question_text: An n x n real matrix A is called real stable if f_A(z) = det(A + diag(z_1,...,z_n)) is a real stable polynomial (nonzero whenever Im(z_i) > 0 for all i). Characterize all real stable n x n matrices.
accepted.context_brief: Characterization of all real stable matrices

evidence.quote: Characterize all real stable n x n matrices, i.e. matrices A such that f_A(z) = det(A+Z) is real stable.

accepted.question_text: For a real entire function phi(x), define the first-order Laguerre expression T_k^{(1)}(phi(x)) = (phi^{(k)}(x))^2 - phi^{(k-1)}(x) phi^{(k+1)}(x) for k >= 1, and the iterated version T_k^{(n)}(phi(x)) = (T_k^{(n-1)}(phi(x)))^2 - T_{k-1}^{(n-1)}(phi(x)) T_{k+1}^{(n-1)}(phi(x)) for n >= 1 and k >= n. If phi(x) is a real entire function of order at most 1 with only real negative zeros, are the iterated Laguerre inequalities T_k^{(n)}(phi(x)) >= 0 valid for all x >= 0 and all k >= n?
accepted.context_brief: Validity of iterated Laguerre inequalities for real entire functions of order at most 1 with only real negative zeros

evidence.quote: If phi(x) is real entire of order at most 1 with only real negative zeros, are the iterated Laguerre inequalities valid for all x >= 0? That is, T_k^{(n)}(phi(x)) >= 0 for all x >= 0 and k >= n?

accepted.question_text: The Hawaii Conjecture: Let p(x) be a real polynomial of degree n >= 2 with exactly 2d nonreal zeros (so 0 <= 2d <= n). Define Q(x) = D(p'(x)/p(x)) where D = d/dx, i.e., Q(x) is the derivative of the logarithmic derivative of p. Let Z_R(Q) denote the number of real zeros of Q counted with multiplicity. Is it true that Z_R(Q(x)) <= 2d?
accepted.context_brief: Hawaii Conjecture: upper bound on real zeros of the derivative of the logarithmic derivative of a real polynomial

evidence.quote: Let p(x) be a real polynomial of degree n >= 2, with exactly 2d nonreal zeros, 0 <= 2d <= n. Let Q(x) = D(p'/p(x)), D = d/dx. The Hawaii conjecture asserts: Z_R(Q(x)) <= 2d, where Z_R(Q) counts real zeros of Q, with multiplicities.

The source states Theorem 1 gives an affirmative answer for the specific functions Xi, Phi, H (defined via the Riemann zeta and Dirichlet L-functions); the general question for arbitrary f is included in q_006 as still open.
